prerequisites: Programming courses, specifically Algorithmics and Computability

learning_outcomes.text: Ability to solve problems within their area of study.
Ability to abstract: ability to create and use models that reflect real situations.
Ability to plan and organize personal work.
Ability to integrate quickly and work efficiently in unidisciplinary teams and to collaborate in a multidisciplinary environment.
Ability for effective oral and written communication (in expression and comprehension), with special emphasis on technical documentation writing.
Possess the necessary learning skills to undertake further studies or improve their training with a certain degree of autonomy.
Have motivation for quality and continuous improvement and act rigorously in professional development.
Knowledge and application of fundamental principles and basic techniques of intelligent systems and their practical application.
Know the fundamentals and application fields of intelligent systems.
Use programming tools for intelligent systems.
Know the main heuristic search algorithms in state spaces and know how to apply them for solving complex problems.
Know and know how to apply other metaheuristics such as evolutionary algorithms for problem solving.
Distinguish the main methods of knowledge representation in artificial intelligence and know how to model problem knowledge with the fastest method.
Know and know how to apply the different inference algorithms associated with the different knowledge representation models.
Know the fundamental methods of knowledge representation and reasoning under uncertainty.
Know some specific methods for problem solving such as action planning, perception or language processing.
Know the fundamentals of computational learning and its scope of application.

syllabus_topics: Vector representation of data and visualization
assessment_rules: In the ordinary sitting, a minimum of 4 out of 10 points is required for both the theory exam and the practice part to pass the subject. If these minimums are met, the final grade is calculated as (0.45 x TEO) + (0.40 x PRA) + (0.10 x TRA) + (0.05 x CUES); otherwise, the grade will be the minimum of the calculated score and 4.0. A final grade of 5 or higher is needed to pass. In the extraordinary sitting, evaluation consists of a theoretical exam and a practical exam. Students who scored 5 or more in either part during the ordinary sitting may only retake the failed part. A minimum of 4 out of 10 points is required for both the theoretical and practical parts. If these minimums are met, the final grade is calculated as (0.50 x Theoretical Exam) + (0.50 x Practical Exam); otherwise, the grade will be the minimum of the calculated score and 4.0. A final grade of 5 or higher is needed to pass. Activities not submitted or completed will be graded as 0. If non-submitted activities exceed 50% of the total weight, the final grade will be "No Presentado" (Absent).
